thread:
Elena: Hey support — embeddings endpoint started returning 1536-dim vectors for a customer that normally uses the 768-dim model. They claim they didn't change anything. Error surfaced after deploy.

Elena: Example: they call /v1/embeddings with model param set to \"embed-lite-768\" and X-Redwood-Project header set to proj_42, but the response vectors are 1536. We also see a different model name in the response metadata.

Elena: Payload (redacted):
```\nPOST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-org_live_abc123
X-Redwood-Project: proj_42
Content-Type: application/json

{ "model": "embed-lite-768", "input": "some text" }
```

Elena: Response snippet: 
```\n200 OK
{"model": "embed-large-1536", "data": [{"embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ... /* 1536 floats */]}]}
```

Elena: Customer says dimension mismatch breaks downstream PCA and similarity code. They flagged billing questions too — looks like usage is billed to the org rather than project.

Maya: Sorry about that, Elena — can you confirm the API key used is an org-level key vs project-level key? Sounds like auth precedence bug.

Elena: Yep, they are using an org key (sk-org_live_abc123). They set X-Redwood-Project explicitly. I told them project key is recommended but they rely on org keys for cross-project access.

Maya: @Sam / @Raj — tagging infra. From the symptoms it sounds like routing picked the org-default model instead of honoring the explicit model/project header. Any recent work on auth routing or model-selection precedence? :thinking:

Sam: I pulled the router logs for that request_ts=1776543209. Decision trace:
```
auth: type=org key org_id=org_7
headers: X-Redwood-Project=proj_42
request.model_hint=embed-lite-768
route_resolution: auth_scope=org_7 -> use default_model=embed-large-1536
```
Sam: So current logic treated the org key as authoritative and chose the org's default model. It didn't check X-Redwood-Project header when auth type=org. That's the bug.

Raj: That's consistent with a recently merged change (PR #1127) that simplified auth precedence. The intent was to prevent project header spoofing, but it overrode explicit project headers entirely when org keys are used.

Maya: Can we confirm if the \"model\" field in body should override routing? Customer explicitly set model param to embed-lite-768. Why was that ignored?

Sam: The routing logic has three tiers (simplified): 1) auth-scoped default (if org key) 2) project config (if project key) 3) request.model param. The PR changed ordering to auth -> request -> project; looks like request.model is only honored for certain key types — bug.

Elena: Customer repro steps attached: 1) use org key, 2) set X-Redwood-Project to proj_42, 3) set model=embed-lite-768 -> result is embed-large-1536.

Maya: Immediate mitigation: ask customer to use a project-scoped key (sk-proj_...) while we patch. Also they can set the model using the query param `?force_model=embed-lite-768` as a temporary knob (internal-only) — if we expose that path it will bypass org-default decision.

Elena: They need a quick workaround — they're on a tight release window. Can we provide the internal knob value and steps?

Sam: I pushed a temporary flag to routing (enable_force_model=true) for the region handling that org. Commands to flip (ops only):
```
# flip for region us-east-1
./control plane set-routing-flag --org org_7 --flag enable_force_model --value true
```
Sam: With that flag on, request.model is honored even for org keys. I've enabled it for org_7.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: routing-flag-change applied to us-east-1 by Sam at 2026-03-15T14:02:10Z

Elena: Verified with customer — they now get 768-dim embeddings. They're happy for now, but want permanent fix and assurance about billing attribution.

Raj: Permanent fix: revert the recent precedence change and add unit tests that cover combinations: org-key + project-header + request.model. Also add an audit log entry indicating which identity (org/project) was used for billing.

Maya: Billing note — current usage for those requests was recorded under org_7. Need to re-attrib if we change routing behavior retroactively. Finance / billing needs a heads-up.

Elena: I'll file a customer update and patch note. Also attaching repro script for Eng:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# repro: shows wrong model selection when using org key
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org_live_abc123" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj_42" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-768","input":"test"}' | jq .
```

Sam: Thanks — I'll open a rollback PR to restore previous precedence and add the missing tests (PR 1189). ETA: hotfix merge + deploy in ~2 hours, full rollout tomorrow after QA.

Maya: I'll loop in Billing (cc finance@) to discuss re-attribution rules if we revert behavior.

Elena: Customer is fine with temporary fix but asks for a postmortem once we have final plan. Please include clear guidance for customers about using org vs project keys.

Raj: Agreed. Postmortem action items I put on the ticket: fix routing precedence, add telemetry that logs model selection reason, expose safe customer-facing knob for forcing model selection, update docs about key types and recommended header usage.

Elena: Awesome, thanks team. Closing the loop with customer now. :thumbsup:

Maya: Marking as escalated -> Eng/Infra. Will update thread when PR merged. :eyes:

Sam: Hotfix merged and staged — deploying to canary now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for routing-service at 2026-03-15T15:01:05Z

Sam: Canary looks good, no regressions in routing tests. Rolling to prod in 30m.

Elena: Customer confirmed no errors in downstream similarity after hotfix. Will follow up for billing.

Maya: Final note to docs: add example curl showing project-scoped key and mention expected billing scope.

Elena: Thanks all.
